profile_name: combo_4 (emphasizes independent exploration+games+creativity, minimizes storytelling+real-life connections)
subject: Mathematics

concept.text: A fraction represents a part of a whole.
concept.visualDemo: Show a drawing on the chalkboard of a circle divided into equal parts, with some parts shaded.

concept.text: The denominator tells us the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into.
concept.misconception: Students often confuse the numerator and denominator, thinking the denominator represents the shaded part.

concept.text: The numerator tells us how many of those equal parts are being considered.
concept.deeperExplanation: This 'consideration' can mean shaded, eaten, selected, etc., depending on the context.

lesson.experience: Divide the class into groups of four. Distribute a small handful of pebbles to each group (around 10-12). Instruct each group to divide their pebbles into two equal piles, then identify what fraction of their total pebbles is in one pile. Next, ask them to take a different number of pebbles from their total and represent that as a fraction of the original total.
expectedSigns: Students in groups are actively dividing pebbles and discussing how to form piles.
Students are correctly identifying the total number of pebbles as the denominator.
Students are using Telugu to verbalize the fraction represented by their selected pebbles (e.g., 'half' or 'two-fifths').
lesson.continuationSuggestion: If signs aren't showing, introduce a game where students draw fractions on their slates based on verbal cues and then compare with a partner.
